subproblems.title: A.e. weighted approximate tangent planes and measurability of tangentProj (Simon Ch. 3, 1.2-1.9)
subproblems.statement: Let n >= 1, l >= 0, U an open subset of R^(n+l), and V = v(M, theta) a RectifiableVarifold n l U: M ⊆ U is H^n-null-measurable and countably n-rectifiable, theta > 0 on M, theta is a.e. measurable for H^n restricted to M, and the integral of theta over M ∩ K is finite for every compact K ⊆ U. Let mu = V.weight = (H^n restricted to M) with density theta and p_x = V.tangentProj x. Then (a) x -> p_x is mu-a.e. strongly measurable; (b) for mu-a.e. x there is a linear subspace T of R^(n+l) which is an approximate tangent space of M with respect to theta at x in the sense of Simon Ch. 3, Def. 1.7 (Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M theta x T, which includes dim T = n), and p_x = T.starProjection is the orthogonal projection onto T.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ), 1 ≤ n → ∀ (U : Set (Amb n ℓ)), IsOpen U → ∀ (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U), AEStronglyMeasurable V.tangentProj V.weight ∧ ∀ᵐ x ∂V.weight, ∃ T : Submodule ℝ (Amb n ℓ), Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n V.carrier V.mult x T ∧ V.tangentProj x = T.starProjection
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Ch. 3, Lemma 1.2 (with Ch. 2, Thm 1.5), Remark 1.3, the proof of Theorem 1.6 ('=>'), Remark 1.8(1) and Theorem 1.9 ('=>'), localized to U (theta is only integrable on compact subsets of U), together with the measurability of the tangent-projection field (Step 7). This is Steps 1-7 of the parent proof (Step 8, the density statement, is not needed here). This child is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.lgc_tangent_plane_ae (DAG node root.lipschitz_graph_corollary-a1.tangent_plane_ae-a1, status accepted, candidate 55e098f5), reused under its byte-identical frozen type; the argument below is the parent's argument specialised to its two conclusions.

Notation: M := V.carrier; theta := V.mult; mu := V.weight; p_x := V.tangentProj x; B_r(x) is the closed ball; H^n = mu_HE[n]; for f in C_c(R^(n+l)), x in R^(n+l) and lambda > 0, Lambda_lambda(f) := integral_{eta_{x,lambda}(M)} f(y) theta(x + lambda y) dH^n(y), where eta_{x,lambda}(z) = (z - x)/lambda. HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M theta x P (SimonGMT Chapter03, Simon Ch. 3, 1.7) means: finrank P = n and Lambda_lambda(f) -> theta(x) integral_P f dH^n as lambda -> 0+ for every f in C_c(R^(n+l)). To prove: (I) x -> p_x is mu-a.e. strongly measurable; (II) for mu-a.e. x there is a subspace T with HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M theta x T and p_x = T.starProjection.

1. Reduction. mu(A) = integral_{A cap M} theta dH^n and theta > 0 on M, so mu(E) = 0 whenever H^n(E cap M) = 0; and mu(R^(n+l) minus M) = 0 (mu is a density measure with respect to H^n restricted to M). Hence a property that holds at every point of M minus E, for a set E with H^n(E) = 0, holds for mu-a.e. x; and a map that agrees with a strongly measurable map at every point of M minus E is mu-a.e. strongly measurable. So it suffices to prove the two conclusions at the points of M minus an H^n-null set. Since U is open, fix open balls W_1, W_2, ... with compact closures cl(W_m) contained in U and union equal to U. Then mu_m := mu restricted to cl(W_m) is a finite Borel regular measure (mu(cl W_m) = integral_{M cap cl W_m} theta dH^n < infinity by V.integrableOn_mult), and it suffices to treat x in M cap W_m for each m. Since theta is H^n-a.e. measurable on M (V.aemeasurable_mult), fix a Borel function theta~ with theta~ = theta almost everywhere for H^n restricted to M; then some Borel set N containing {theta != theta~} has (H^n restricted to M)(N) = H^n(N cap M) = 0, so N_theta := {x in M : theta(x) != theta~(x)}, which is contained in N cap M, is an H^n-null set.

2. C^1 cover (Simon Ch. 3, Lemma 1.2). By V.countablyRectifiable, M is contained in M_0' union (union over j of F_j(R^n)) with H^n(M_0') = 0 and F_j : R^n -> R^(n+l) Lipschitz.
 (2a) C^1 approximation (Simon Ch. 2, Thm 1.5, applied to each coordinate function; printed proof): let F : R^n -> R be Lipschitz and epsilon > 0. By Rademacher's theorem (SimonGMT Chapter02.rademacher_ae_differentiableAt) F is differentiable on a set B with L^n(R^n minus B) = 0. By Lusin's theorem there is a closed set C contained in B with grad F restricted to C continuous and L^n(R^n minus C) < epsilon/2. For x, y in C let R(x,y) := (F(y) - F(x) - grad F(x).(y - x))/|x - y| and eta_k(x) := sup{|R(x,y)| : y in C cap B_{1/k}(x), y != x}; eta_k decreases to 0 pointwise on C (differentiability), so by Egoroff's theorem on the sets C cap B_j(0) there is a closed set A contained in C with L^n(R^n minus A) < epsilon on whose bounded subsets eta_k -> 0 uniformly, i.e. Whitney's condition 1.6(*) holds on A. Whitney's extension theorem (Simon Ch. 2, Thm 1.6; SimonGMT Chapter02.exists_contDiff_one_extension_of_whitney) gives g in C^1(R^n) with g = F and grad g = grad F on A, so L^n({F != g}) < epsilon.
 (2b) Hence for each j and i >= 1 there is G_ij in C^1(R^n; R^(n+l)) with L^n({F_j != G_ij}) < 1/i. With Z_j := R^n minus (union over i of {F_j = G_ij}) we get L^n(Z_j) = 0, hence H^n(F_j(Z_j)) <= (Lip F_j)^n L^n(Z_j) = 0, and F_j(R^n) is contained in F_j(Z_j) union (union over i of G_ij(R^n)).
 (2c) For a C^1 map G : R^n -> R^(n+l) let JG := sqrt(det(DG^T DG)); JG(v) = 0 iff DG(v) is not injective. The image of the critical set {JG = 0} is H^n-null (Sard-type consequence of the area formula; SimonGMT Chapter02.area_image_criticalSet_eq_zero). If JG(v) > 0, then by the inverse function theorem (applied at (v, 0) to the C^1 map (w, t) -> G(w) + L t of R^n x R^l, where L is a linear isomorphism of R^l onto a complement of DG(v)(R^n), whose differential at (v, 0) is invertible) there is r_v > 0 such that G is injective with injective differential on B_{2 r_v}(v) and G restricted to B^o_{2 r_v}(v) is a homeomorphism onto its image; then N := G(B^o_{r_v}(v)) is an embedded n-dimensional C^1 submanifold, it is sigma-compact (union of the compact sets G(B_{r_v - 1/k}(v))) hence Borel, H^n(N) <= integral_{B_{r_v}(v)} JG dL^n < infinity (area formula for the injective Lipschitz map G on B_{r_v}(v); SimonGMT Chapter02.injective_area_formula_lipschitz_simon), T_z N = DG(w)(R^n) for z = G(w), and z -> p_{T_z N} = DG(w)(DG(w)^T DG(w))^(-1) DG(w)^T with w = G^(-1)(z) is continuous on N. By the Lindelof property countably many such balls cover {JG > 0}.
 (2d) Collecting: M is contained in N_0 union (union over j >= 1 of N_j), where N_0 is a Borel set with H^n(N_0) = 0 (enlarge the null set to a Borel null set, H^n being Borel regular) and each N_j (j >= 1) is a Borel embedded n-dimensional C^1 submanifold with H^n(N_j) < infinity on which z -> p_{T_z N_j} is continuous.

3. Disjoint pieces (Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.3; SimonGMT Chapter03.simon_remark_1_3_nullMeasurable). Put M_0 := M cap N_0 and M_j := (M cap N_j) minus (union over i < j of N_i) for j >= 1. These sets are pairwise disjoint and H^n-null-measurable (M is, the N_i are Borel), M is their union, H^n(M_0) = 0, and M_j is contained in N_j.

4. Blow-up of a C^1 submanifold. Let N be one of the N_j and x in N. Claim: for every f in C_c(R^(n+l)), lambda^(-n) integral_N f((z - x)/lambda) dH^n(z) -> integral_{T_x N} f dH^n as lambda -> 0+, and for each R > 0 the quantity lambda^(-n) H^n(N cap B_{R lambda}(x)) stays bounded as lambda -> 0+. Proof: choose an orthogonal map Q of R^(n+l) with Q(T_x N) = R^n x {0}. By the implicit function theorem (applied in a local parametrization G of N to w -> p_{T_x N}(G(w) - x), whose differential at G^(-1)(x) is invertible) there are r > 0, an open set W containing x and a C^1 map u : B^n_r(0) -> R^l with u(0) = 0, Du(0) = 0 and N cap W = {x + Q^(-1)(v, u(v)) : v in B^n_r(0)}; shrinking r (and W with it) we may assume that u is C^1 on a neighbourhood of the closed ball B^n_r(0), so that u and Du are bounded there and u is Lipschitz on B^n_r(0); as N is embedded there is epsilon > 0 with N cap B_epsilon(x) contained in N cap W. Let f be supported in B_R(0) and 0 < lambda < epsilon/R. By the area formula for the injective Lipschitz graph map v -> (v, u(v)) (Jacobian J_u(v) = sqrt(det(I + Du(v)^T Du(v))), continuous with J_u(0) = 1) and the substitution v = lambda w,
 lambda^(-n) integral_N f((z - x)/lambda) dH^n(z) = integral_{B^n_{r/lambda}(0)} f(Q^(-1)(w, u(lambda w)/lambda)) J_u(lambda w) dw.
The integrand vanishes for |w| > R, and for |w| <= R we have u(lambda w)/lambda -> Du(0) w = 0 and J_u(lambda w) -> 1 uniformly, while f is bounded and uniformly continuous; hence the right side tends to integral_{R^n} f(Q^(-1)(w, 0)) dw = integral_{T_x N} f dH^n (H^n on the n-plane T_x N is the image of L^n under the isometry w -> Q^(-1)(w, 0); Mathlib normalizes mu_HE[n] to agree with volume on EuclideanSpace R (Fin n)). For the boundedness claim choose f in C_c(R^(n+l)) with 0 <= f <= 1, f = 1 on B_R(0) and f = 0 off B_{R+1}(0); then lambda^(-n) H^n(N cap B_{R lambda}(x)) <= lambda^(-n) integral_N f((z - x)/lambda) dH^n(z) (the integrand is >= 1 on N cap B_{R lambda}(x) and >= 0 elsewhere), and the right side converges as lambda -> 0+ by the first claim (applied with R + 1 in place of R), so it is bounded for all small lambda > 0.

5. Lusin sets and upper-density sets (Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.8(1)). Fix j >= 1 and m and put A_{j,m} := (M_j cap W_m) minus N_theta, so H^n(A_{j,m}) <= H^n(N_j) < infinity. By Lusin's theorem (Simon Ch. 1, 1.17; SimonGMT Chapter01 IsBorelRegularOuterMeasure.simon_theorem_1_17; H^n is Borel regular) applied to the Borel function theta~ on A_{j,m}, for each k there is a closed set K_{j,m,k} contained in A_{j,m} with H^n(A_{j,m} minus K_{j,m,k}) < 1/k and theta~ restricted to K_{j,m,k} continuous (Lusin applies: A_{j,m} is H^n-measurable, being the H^n-null-measurable set M_j cap W_m minus the H^n-null set N_theta, and H^n(A_{j,m}) < infinity); since K_{j,m,k} is contained in the bounded ball W_m, it is closed and bounded, hence compact; on K_{j,m,k} we have theta = theta~, so theta restricted to K_{j,m,k} is continuous, and H^n(A_{j,m} minus (union over k of K_{j,m,k})) = 0. By the upper density theorem (Simon Ch. 1, Thm 3.6; SimonGMT Chapter01.simon_theorem_3_6), writing K := K_{j,m,k}:
 (i) applied to the finite Borel regular measure mu_m and the mu_m-measurable set M minus K: limsup_{lambda -> 0+} lambda^(-n) mu_m((M minus K) cap B_lambda(x)) = 0 for H^n-a.e. x outside M minus K, in particular for H^n-a.e. x in K;
 (ii) applied to the finite Borel regular measure H^n restricted to N_j (finite since H^n(N_j) < infinity) and the H^n-measurable set N_j minus K (N_j is Borel and K is compact): limsup_{lambda -> 0+} lambda^(-n) H^n((N_j minus K) cap B_lambda(x)) = 0 for H^n-a.e. x in K.
Let E be the union, over all j >= 1, m, k, of the exceptional H^n-null sets of (i) and (ii) and of the sets A_{j,m} minus (union over k of K_{j,m,k}), together with M_0 and N_theta. Then H^n(E) = 0, and every x in M minus E lies in some K_{j,m,k}.

6. Existence of the weighted approximate tangent space (proof of Thm 1.6 '=>' combined with Remark 1.8(1), i.e. Thm 1.9 '=>'). Let x in M minus E, so x in K := K_{j,m,k}, contained in M_j cap W_m, for some j >= 1, m, k. Put P := T_x N_j, an n-dimensional subspace. Let f in C_c(R^(n+l)) be supported in B_R(0), and let lambda > 0 be so small that B_{R lambda}(x) is contained in W_m. The homothety z -> (z - x)/lambda maps H^n restricted to M onto lambda^n times H^n restricted to eta_{x,lambda}(M) (scaling law H^n(x + lambda S) = lambda^n H^n(S); Mathlib hausdorffMeasure_homothety_image), so y -> theta(x + lambda y) is a.e. measurable for H^n restricted to eta_{x,lambda}(M) (composition of the a.e.-measurable theta with this homothety), the integrand y -> f(y) theta(x + lambda y) is integrable there (bounded by sup|f| times theta(x + lambda y) on the blow-up of M cap B_{R lambda}(x), and integral_{M cap B_{R lambda}(x)} theta dH^n < infinity), and
 Lambda_lambda(f) = lambda^(-n) integral_M f((z - x)/lambda) theta(z) dH^n(z).
The integrand z -> f((z - x)/lambda) theta(z) on M is integrable for H^n restricted to M (it is a.e. strongly measurable, vanishes off the compact ball B_{R lambda}(x) contained in U, and is bounded by sup|f| theta, which is integrable on M cap B_{R lambda}(x)), and z -> f((z - x)/lambda) is bounded and continuous, hence integrable on the sets K and N_j of finite H^n-measure; so the following splittings of Bochner integrals are legitimate. Split M as K union (M minus K) (K is compact, hence Borel):
 (a) |lambda^(-n) integral_{M minus K} f((z - x)/lambda) theta(z) dH^n(z)| <= sup|f| lambda^(-n) mu((M minus K) cap B_{R lambda}(x)) = sup|f| R^n (R lambda)^(-n) mu_m((M minus K) cap B_{R lambda}(x)) -> 0 by 5(i) (B_{R lambda}(x) is contained in W_m, where mu and mu_m agree, and theta > 0 on M);
 (b) |lambda^(-n) integral_K f((z - x)/lambda) (theta(z) - theta(x)) dH^n(z)| <= sup|f| e(lambda) lambda^(-n) H^n(N_j cap B_{R lambda}(x)) -> 0, where e(lambda) := sup{|theta(z) - theta(x)| : z in K cap B_{R lambda}(x)} -> 0 by continuity of theta on K at x, and the last factor is bounded by Step 4;
 (c) theta(x) lambda^(-n) integral_K f((z - x)/lambda) dH^n(z) = theta(x) [lambda^(-n) integral_{N_j} f((z - x)/lambda) dH^n(z) - lambda^(-n) integral_{N_j minus K} f((z - x)/lambda) dH^n(z)] -> theta(x) [integral_P f dH^n - 0] by Step 4 and 5(ii).
Adding (a), (b), (c): Lambda_lambda(f) -> theta(x) integral_P f dH^n as lambda -> 0+. Together with finrank P = n this is exactly HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M theta x P. Since theta(x) > 0 (x in M), weighted approximate tangent spaces at x are unique (SimonGMT Chapter03.HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique), and the condition 'there is a subspace Q with HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M theta x Q' in the definition of V.tangentProj holds (with Q = P); hence V.tangentProj x is the starProjection of the chosen witness, which equals P by uniqueness, i.e. p_x = P.starProjection, the orthogonal projection onto the n-dimensional subspace P = T_x N_j. Thus T := P satisfies HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M theta x T and V.tangentProj x = T.starProjection at every x in M minus E. Since H^n(E) = 0, Step 1 shows that this holds for mu-a.e. x, which is the second conclusion.

7. Measurability. For each j >= 1 choose a Borel set B_j contained in M_j with H^n(M_j minus B_j) = 0 (M_j is H^n-null-measurable). Define q(x) := p_{T_x N_j} if x in B_j (j >= 1) and q(x) := 0 otherwise. Each map x -> p_{T_x N_j} is continuous on the Borel set N_j (Step 2) and the B_j are pairwise disjoint Borel sets, so q is Borel measurable; its values lie in the finite-dimensional, hence second countable, normed space of linear maps of R^(n+l), so q is strongly measurable. By Step 6, p_x = p_{T_x N_j} = q(x) for every x in B_j minus E, and M minus (union over j >= 1 of (B_j minus E)) is H^n-null. By Step 1, p = q mu-a.e., so x -> p_x = V.tangentProj x is AEStronglyMeasurable with respect to mu = V.weight, which is the first conclusion. Both conjuncts are proved.
proof_key_steps: Reduction: mu << H^n restricted to M and mu(complement of M) = 0, so it suffices to work at H^n-a.e. x in M; localize to balls W_m with compact closure in U and fix a Borel representative theta~ of theta (null set N_theta).

Lemma 1.2 with the printed proof of the C^1 approximation theorem (Ch. 2, Thm 1.5): M is covered, up to an H^n-null Borel set, by countably many Borel embedded C^1 n-submanifolds N_j with H^n(N_j) < infinity and continuous tangent projections.
Remark 1.3: disjoint H^n-null-measurable pieces M_j contained in N_j.
Blow-ups of a C^1 submanifold at x converge to H^n on T_x N, with bounded local density.
Lusin compacts K with theta continuous on K, and upper-density estimates for mu restricted to M minus K and for H^n restricted to N_j minus K.

At every x in M minus an H^n-null set E the weighted blow-ups converge to theta(x) times integration over P = T_x N_j, so HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M theta x P; uniqueness (theta(x) > 0) and the definition of tangentProj give p_x = P.starProjection.
p agrees mu-a.e. with the Borel map assembled from the continuous maps x -> p_{T_x N_j} on Borel cores B_j of M_j, hence is AEStronglyMeasurable.
Since H^n(E) = 0 and mu << H^n restricted to M, both conclusions hold mu-a.e.

subproblems.title: Real density limit at a weighted approximate tangent point (Simon 3.1.8(2))
subproblems.statement: Let n ≥ 1 and U ⊆ ℝ^{n+ℓ} open. Let V = v(M, θ) be a RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U, x ∈ U, and P a subspace with Chapter03.HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x P. Then r⁻ⁿ ∫_{M ∩ B_r(x)} θ dHⁿ → ω_n·θ(x) in ℝ as r ↓ 0 (along 𝓝[>] 0). Here B_r(x) is the closed ball, Hⁿ = μHE[n] and ω_n = unitBallVolume n.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ), 1 ≤ n → ∀ (U : Set (Amb n ℓ)), IsOpen U → ∀ (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U) (x : Amb n ℓ) (P : Submodule ℝ (Amb n ℓ)), x ∈ U → Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n V.carrier V.mult x P → Tendsto (fun r : ℝ => (r ^ n)⁻¹ * ∫ z in V.carrier ∩ closedBall x r, V.mult z ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Amb n ℓ))) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 (unitBallVolume n * V.mult x))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Ch. 3, Remark 1.8(2); this is the squeeze part of Step 8 of the parent proof, made self-contained and stated for a point x of U (the parent applies it at points of M). This child is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.rsod_tendsto_scaled_mult_integral (DAG node root.regular_set_open_dense-a1.density_of_approx_tangent-a1.scaled_mult_integral_limit-a1, status accepted since 2026-10-12T09:51:49Z, candidate b30ebfa8), reused under its byte-identical frozen type. (The parent text cites Mathlib EuclideanSpace.volume_ball for omega_n; that lemma is outside the frozen contract's import closure, so Fact B below computes the plane-ball measure directly.)

Notation: M := V.carrier, theta := V.mult, H := H^n = mu_HE[n], omega := unitBallVolume n = pi^(n/2)/Gamma(n/2+1), t := theta(x), eta_r := blowUpMap x r, eta_r(z) = r^(-1)(z - x). For phi in C_c(R^(n+l), R) and r > 0 put Lambda_r(phi) := integral_{eta_r(M)} phi(y) theta(x + r y) dH(y), I(r) := integral_{M cap closedBall x r} theta dH and J(r) := (r^n)^(-1) I(r) (real Bochner integrals). The hypothesis HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M theta x P means: finrank P = n and, for every phi in C_c(R^(n+l), R), Lambda_r(phi) -> t integral_P phi dH as r -> 0+ (along the filter of right neighbourhoods of 0). Goal: J(r) -> omega t as r -> 0+.

Fact A (blow-up change of variables). For every r > 0 and every function phi: Lambda_r(phi) = (r^n)^(-1) integral_M phi(eta_r(z)) theta(z) dH(z). Proof: eta_r is a homeomorphism (translation by -x, then dilation by r^(-1) != 0), hence a bijective measurable embedding with inverse y -> x + r y. For every set S, H(eta_r(S)) = (r^(-1))^n H(S), because translations preserve H and the homothety of ratio r^(-1) multiplies H by (r^(-1))^n (Mathlib euclideanHausdorffMeasure_homothety_image). Since eta_r is bijective, A cap eta_r(M) = eta_r(eta_r^(-1)(A) cap M) for measurable A, so H restricted to eta_r(M) equals (r^(-1))^n times the push-forward of H restricted to M under eta_r. Transporting the Bochner integral (integral_smul_measure and MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map, neither of which needs integrability) gives integral_{eta_r(M)} g dH = (r^(-1))^n integral_M g(eta_r(z)) dH(z) for every g; with g(y) = phi(y) theta(x + r y) we have g(eta_r(z)) = phi(eta_r(z)) theta(z), and (r^(-1))^n = (r^n)^(-1).

Fact B (H^n of balls in the n-plane P). For every s >= 0, (H restricted to P)(closedBall 0 s) = ofReal(omega s^n). Proof: the inclusion of P is a linear isometry, so H restricted to P is the push-forward of the n-dimensional Hausdorff measure of P, and the preimage of closedBall 0 s is the closed s-ball of P. On the n-dimensional inner product space P (finrank P = n), H^n equals Lebesgue measure (InnerProductSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume), so the measure is s^n times the volume of the unit ball of P (Measure.addHaar_closedBall). That volume is omega: computing integral_P e^(-|y|^2) dy in orthonormal coordinates gives pi^(n/2) (Tonelli and integral_R e^(-u^2) du = sqrt(pi)), while the layer-cake formula ({e^(-|y|^2) > s'} is the ball of radius sqrt(-log s') for 0 < s' < 1 and is empty for s' >= 1) together with the substitution s' = e^(-u) gives volume(unit ball) times integral_0^infinity u^(n/2) e^(-u) du = volume(unit ball) Gamma(n/2 + 1) (the set is empty for s' >= 1, so only 0 < s' < 1 contributes); as Gamma(n/2 + 1) > 0, the unit ball has volume pi^(n/2)/Gamma(n/2 + 1) = omega.

1. Constants and radius. omega > 0, because pi^(n/2) > 0 and Gamma(n/2 + 1) > 0. Since x is in U and U is open, there is eps0 > 0 with ball x eps0 contained in U; put delta := eps0/4 > 0. For every s < eps0, closedBall x s is contained in ball x eps0, hence in U, and it is compact, so theta is H-integrable on M cap closedBall x s (V.integrableOn_mult).

2. Blow-up geometry. For r > 0 and every z, |eta_r(z)| = r^(-1)|z - x| = dist(z, x)/r. Hence |eta_r(z)| <= 1 iff z is in closedBall x r, and |eta_r(z)| >= c iff dist(z, x) >= c r (c > 0). The map eta_r is continuous.

3. Cutoffs. For 0 < a < b let g_{a,b}(y) := min(1, max(0, (b - |y|)/(b - a))). Then g_{a,b} is continuous, 0 <= g_{a,b} <= 1, g_{a,b}(y) = 1 when |y| <= a, and g_{a,b}(y) = 0 when |y| >= b. So g_{a,b} vanishes outside the compact set closedBall 0 b and defines an element of C_c(R^(n+l), R).

4. Comparison lemma. Let phi be in C_c(R^(n+l), R) with 0 <= phi <= 1 and phi(y) = 0 whenever |y| >= 2, and let 0 < r < delta. Then
 (U) if phi(y) = 1 whenever |y| <= 1, then J(r) <= Lambda_r(phi);
 (L) if phi(y) = 0 whenever |y| >= 1, then Lambda_r(phi) <= J(r).
Proof. Put S := M cap closedBall x (2r). As 2r < eps0, theta is H-integrable on S (Step 1), and S is H-null-measurable (M is, by V.nullMeasurableSet_carrier, and the ball is closed).
 (a) By Fact A, Lambda_r(phi) = (r^n)^(-1) integral_M phi(eta_r(z)) theta(z) dH(z).
 (b) If z is in M but not in S, then dist(z, x) > 2r, so |eta_r(z)| >= 2 and phi(eta_r(z)) theta(z) = 0. Since M is H-null-measurable and S is contained in M, integral_M phi(eta_r(z)) theta(z) dH = integral_S phi(eta_r(z)) theta(z) dH (Mathlib setIntegral_eq_of_subset_of_ae_sdiff_eq_zero).
 (c) I(r) = integral_S 1_{closedBall x r}(z) theta(z) dH(z): the integral of the indicator of the measurable set closedBall x r over S is the integral over closedBall x r cap S, and closedBall x r cap S = M cap closedBall x r because closedBall x r is contained in closedBall x (2r).
 (d) Both z -> 1_{closedBall x r}(z) theta(z) and z -> phi(eta_r(z)) theta(z) are integrable for H restricted to S: the first is the indicator of a measurable set times an integrable function; for the second, phi o eta_r is continuous and theta is a.e. strongly measurable for H restricted to S (being integrable there), so the product is a.e. strongly measurable, and |phi(eta_r(z)) theta(z)| <= |theta(z)|.
 (e) For H-restricted-to-S-a.e. z we have z in S, so z in M and theta(z) > 0 (V.mult_pos). In case (U): if z is in closedBall x r then |eta_r(z)| <= 1, so phi(eta_r(z)) theta(z) = theta(z) = 1_{closedBall x r}(z) theta(z); otherwise 1_{closedBall x r}(z) theta(z) = 0 <= phi(eta_r(z)) theta(z). In case (L): if z is in closedBall x r then phi(eta_r(z)) theta(z) <= theta(z) = 1_{closedBall x r}(z) theta(z) (phi <= 1, theta(z) > 0); otherwise dist(z, x) > r, so |eta_r(z)| >= 1 and phi(eta_r(z)) theta(z) = 0 = 1_{closedBall x r}(z) theta(z).
 (f) Integrating the a.e. inequality of (e) over S (monotonicity of the integral of integrable functions, by (d)), multiplying by (r^n)^(-1) >= 0 and using (a), (b), (c) gives (U) and (L).

5. Plane integrals. By the hypothesis finrank P = n, so Fact B gives (H restricted to P)(closedBall 0 s) = ofReal(omega s^n) for every s >= 0. In particular this measure is finite, so 1_{closedBall 0 s} is integrable for H restricted to P and integral_P 1_{closedBall 0 s} dH = omega s^n. Consequently, for phi in C_c(R^(n+l), R) with 0 <= phi <= 1:
 (U') if s >= 0 and phi(y) = 0 whenever |y| >= s, then phi <= 1_{closedBall 0 s} pointwise and, as phi >= 0, integral_P phi dH <= omega s^n (integral_mono_of_nonneg);
 (L') if s, s' >= 0, phi(y) = 1 whenever |y| <= s and phi(y) = 0 whenever |y| >= s', then phi is integrable for H restricted to P (continuous and |phi| <= 1_{closedBall 0 s'}, which is integrable) and 1_{closedBall 0 s} <= phi pointwise, so omega s^n <= integral_P phi dH.

6. t >= 0. Let phi_0 := g_{1/2,1}. For every r > 0, Fact A gives Lambda_r(phi_0) = (r^n)^(-1) integral_M phi_0(eta_r(z)) theta(z) dH(z), and the integrand is >= 0 at every point of M (phi_0 >= 0 and theta > 0 on M), hence a.e. for H restricted to M (a.e. point lies in the null-measurable set M); so Lambda_r(phi_0) >= 0 (the Bochner integral of an a.e. nonnegative function is nonnegative). By the hypothesis, Lambda_r(phi_0) -> t integral_P phi_0 dH as r -> 0+; since the filter of right neighbourhoods of 0 is nontrivial and Lambda_r(phi_0) >= 0 for all r > 0, the limit is >= 0 (ge_of_tendsto), i.e. t integral_P phi_0 dH >= 0. By 5(L') with s = 1/2 and s' = 1, integral_P phi_0 dH >= omega 2^(-n) > 0. Hence t >= 0.

7. Squeeze. We check the two order conditions characterizing J(r) -> omega t in R.
 (i) Let a < omega t. The map e -> t omega (1 - e)^n is continuous with value t omega at e = 0, so there is e with 0 < e < 1 and a < t omega (1 - e)^n. Let phi_- := g_{1-e,1}: 0 <= phi_- <= 1, phi_-(y) = 1 for |y| <= 1 - e, phi_-(y) = 0 for |y| >= 1 (hence for |y| >= 2). By 5(L') (s = 1 - e, s' = 1) and t >= 0, t integral_P phi_- dH >= t omega (1 - e)^n > a. By the hypothesis, Lambda_r(phi_-) -> t integral_P phi_- dH, so Lambda_r(phi_-) > a for all sufficiently small r > 0; also r lies in (0, delta) for all sufficiently small r > 0, and then 4(L) gives Lambda_r(phi_-) <= J(r). Hence a < J(r) for all sufficiently small r > 0.
 (ii) Let b > omega t. Choose e with 0 < e < 1 and t omega (1 + e)^n < b (continuity at e = 0), and let phi_+ := g_{1,1+e}: 0 <= phi_+ <= 1, phi_+(y) = 1 for |y| <= 1, phi_+(y) = 0 for |y| >= 1 + e, hence for |y| >= 2 since e < 1. By 5(U') (s = 1 + e) and t >= 0, t integral_P phi_+ dH <= t omega (1 + e)^n < b. By the hypothesis, Lambda_r(phi_+) < b for all sufficiently small r > 0, and for r in (0, delta), 4(U) gives J(r) <= Lambda_r(phi_+). Hence J(r) < b for all sufficiently small r > 0.

8. By (i) and (ii) and the order-topology characterization of limits in R (tendsto_order), J(r) = (r^n)^(-1) integral_{M cap closedBall x r} theta dH^n -> omega t = unitBallVolume n * theta(x) as r -> 0+.
proof_key_steps: omega_n > 0; choose delta > 0 with closedBall x (4 delta) inside U (x in U, U open), so theta is H^n-integrable on M cap closedBall x s for s < 4 delta.

Fact A: blow-up change of variables Lambda_r(phi) = r^(-n) integral_M phi(eta_r z) theta(z) dH^n (homothety scaling of H^n); Fact B: H^n(P cap closedBall 0 s) = omega_n s^n (H^n = Lebesgue on the n-plane, unit-ball volume via the Gaussian integral).
Cutoffs g_{a,b} in C_c with 0 <= g <= 1, g = 1 on |y| <= a, g = 0 on |y| >= b; |eta_r z| = dist(z,x)/r.

Comparison for 0 < r < delta: J(r) <= Lambda_r(phi) when phi = 1 on the unit ball, Lambda_r(phi) <= J(r) when phi vanishes off the open unit ball (localize to M cap closedBall x (2r), integrability, theta > 0 on M).
Plane bounds: integral_P g_{1-e,1} >= omega_n (1-e)^n and integral_P g_{1,1+e} <= omega_n (1+e)^n.
theta(x) >= 0 from Lambda_r(g_{1/2,1}) >= 0 and its limit theta(x) integral_P g_{1/2,1} with positive plane integral.
Order-topology squeeze: for every a < omega_n theta(x) < b, eventually a < J(r) < b, so J(r) -> omega_n theta(x).

subproblems.title: Weight of a closed ball as the integral of the multiplicity
subproblems.statement: Let n, ℓ ∈ ℕ and U ⊆ ℝ^{n+ℓ}. Let V = v(M, θ) be a rectifiable n-varifold in U (RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U) with carrier M and multiplicity θ. Let x ∈ ℝ^{n+ℓ} and r ∈ ℝ be such that the closed ball B_r(x) ⊆ U. Then μ_V(B_r(x)) = ENNReal.ofReal(∫_{M ∩ B_r(x)} θ dHⁿ), where Hⁿ = μHE[n].
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (U : Set (Amb n ℓ)) (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U) (x : Amb n ℓ) (r : ℝ), closedBall x r ⊆ U → V.weight (closedBall x r) = ENNReal.ofReal (∫ z in V.carrier ∩ closedBall x r, V.mult z ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Amb n ℓ)))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 4, 1.1 (mu_V = H^n restricted to M with density theta). This child is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.rsod_weight_closedBall_eq_ofReal_integral (DAG node root.regular_set_open_dense-a1.density_of_approx_tangent-a1.weight_ball_integral-a1, status accepted, candidate 02c3706f), reused under its byte-identical frozen type; it is the identity mu(B_lambda(x)) = integral_{M cap B_lambda(x)} theta dH^n used in Step 8 of the parent proof (to identify lambda^(-n) integral_{M cap B_lambda(x)} theta dH^n with lambda^(-n) mu(B_lambda(x))).

Notation: M := V.carrier, theta := V.mult, H := H^n = mu_HE[n], B := closedBall x r, with B contained in U.

1. Integrability. B is compact (closed and bounded in the finite-dimensional space R^(n+l)) and B is contained in U, so theta is H-integrable on M cap B by V.integrableOn_mult.
2. Sign. M is H-null-measurable (V.nullMeasurableSet_carrier) and B is closed, so M cap B is H-null-measurable and H-a.e. point of M cap B (for H restricted to M cap B) lies in M cap B (ae_restrict_mem0); there theta > 0 by V.mult_pos. Hence theta >= 0 a.e. for H restricted to M cap B.
3. Computation. By definition V.weight = (H restricted to M).withDensity(z -> ofReal(theta(z))). Since B is measurable, V.weight(B) = integral^- over B of ofReal(theta) d(H restricted to M) (withDensity_apply) = integral^- of ofReal(theta) d(H restricted to B cap M) (Measure.restrict_restrict) = integral^- over M cap B of ofReal(theta) dH. By Steps 1 and 2 and ofReal_integral_eq_lintegral_ofReal, this lower integral equals ofReal(integral_{M cap B} theta dH). Hence V.weight(closedBall x r) = ofReal(integral_{M cap closedBall x r} theta dH^n).
proof_key_steps: theta is H^n-integrable on M cap B since B is compact and contained in U (V.integrableOn_mult).
theta >= 0 a.e. on M cap B because theta > 0 on M and a.e. point of the null-measurable set M cap B lies in it.
Unfold V.weight as a withDensity of H^n restricted to M, restrict to B, and convert the lower integral to ofReal of the Bochner integral.
